h1: The 5 Best Greenworks Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Greenworks Leaf Blowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five cordless Greenworks leaf blowers across 40V, 60V and 80V platforms, compared by airflow in CFM and price bucket.
summary: The Greenworks 80V blower rated at 770 CFM is our pick for big yards. A second 80V model at 730 CFM costs a bucket less, a 40V model matches that airflow, the 60V suits mid-size yards, and the 40V 500 CFM is the cheap starter.
intro: Greenworks sells the same blower idea across 40V, 60V and 80V batteries, and the voltage on the box does not predict airflow. A 40V model here moves as much air as an 80V one, which catches people choosing by volts.

We reviewed five cordless Greenworks blowers and ranked them on listed CFM and price bucket. Our facts do not include battery runtime, weight or what ships in the box, so check the live listing for those, especially whether a battery is included.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (770 CFM)
products.verdict: The highest airflow in the group at 770 CFM.
products.description:
This Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower lists 770 CFM of airflow in a cordless design, in the $200-500 bucket.

It takes first place for moving the most air of the five. The cost is a higher bucket than the 80V 730 CFM model just below.

Get it for large yards with heavy leaf piles. Runtime and weight are not in our facts.
products.idealFor: Large yards and heavy leaf cleanup.

products.name: Greenworks 80V Electric Leaf Blower (730 CFM)
products.verdict: 730 CFM from a lower price bucket than the leader.
products.description:
This Greenworks 80V blower lists 730 CFM and cordless operation, in the $100-200 bucket.

Second place is because it gives up only 40 CFM against the 770 model while dropping a full price bucket. That is the best airflow-per-dollar in this ranking.

Buy it if you want near-top airflow for less. Confirm what is included in the box.
products.idealFor: Big yards on a smaller budget.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Electric Leaf Blower (730 CFM)
products.verdict: A 40V model matching the 80V airflow, in a higher bucket.
products.description:
This Greenworks 40V blower lists 730 CFM and cordless use, in the $200-500 bucket.

Third place reflects the price: it matches the 80V 730 CFM airflow but sits in a higher bucket. The 40V platform could suit owners with existing 40V batteries.

Buy it if you already own 40V gear. Otherwise the cheaper 80V does the same job.

products.name: Greenworks 60V Electric Leaf Blower (610 CFM)
products.description:
This Greenworks 60V blower lists 610 CFM and cordless operation, in the $200-500 bucket.

It lands fourth because it delivers less airflow than the 730 and 770 models while costing more than the 80V 730 CFM one. The 60V platform is its only distinguishing trait.

Buy it if you own 60V tools. Everyone else gets more air for less elsewhere.
products.skipIf: You want the best airflow per dollar.

products.name: Greenworks 40V Cordless Leaf Blower (500 CFM)
products.verdict: 500 CFM at a lower price for small yards.
products.description:
This Greenworks 40V Cordless Leaf Blower lists 500 CFM, in the $100-200 bucket.

It finishes last on raw airflow, with the lowest CFM here, but it shares the lower bucket with the 80V 730 CFM model.

Buy it for light cleanup on small yards and patios. For bigger jobs it will feel underpowered.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is the volume of air the blower moves per minute. It matters because it tracks how big a leaf pile you can shift. Look for the CFM number in the title or bullets.
Voltage names the battery platform. It matters because 40V, 60V and 80V batteries do not swap, so you want the one matching your other tools. Do not assume higher volts means more air.
Buckets here range from $100-200 to $200-500. It matters because equal airflow appears in both. Compare CFM first and pay extra only for a reason.
Some listings include the battery and charger, others sell the tool alone. It matters because a battery adds a lot to the real cost. Read the box contents line.
A small yard needs less airflow than an acre. It matters because buying too much wastes money. Match CFM to your biggest cleanup job.

faq.q: Does higher voltage mean more airflow?
faq.a: No. The 40V 730 CFM model matches an 80V one on airflow.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Buying by voltage alone. Compare CFM and price bucket.

faq.q: Is the 770 CFM model worth it over the 730?
faq.a: Only for the biggest yards. The 730 CFM 80V model costs a bucket less.

faq.q: Do batteries come in the box?
faq.a: Our facts do not say. Check each listing.

faq.q: How do I maintain a cordless blower?
faq.a: Clean the intake and store the battery per the manual.

faq.q: Can I use 40V batteries in an 80V blower?
faq.a: No. Battery platforms differ, so match voltage.

finalTake: The 80V 730 CFM Greenworks is the best-value pick for most yards, with the 770 CFM model for maximum air. Choose the 40V models if you already own that battery, and the 500 CFM unit for small spaces.
